mechanism_narrative: Low levels of the federal funds rate indicate an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity. This effect is expected to positively influence S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS levels, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 10% signals labor market weakness, which can lead to decreased consumer spending and negative impacts on corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following a significant UNRATE increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is falling, it indicates a tightening labor market and potential monetary policy tightening, which can lead to increased borrowing costs and negative equity market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following rising FEDFUNDS and falling UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a strong economy, which is typically positive for corporate earnings and equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following positive GDP growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals increased economic activity and supply, which is typically positive for equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following increased industrial production, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates reduced consumer demand, which can lead to negative impacts on corporate revenues and equity markets, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following a decline in RSAFS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is rising and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is also rising, it indicates inflationary pressures and potential monetary policy tightening, which can lead to negative equity market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following rising CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which is typically positive for consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows following payroll growth, the hypothesis is rejected.
